GUIDE.TITLE: User Guide
GUIDE.SUBTITLE: Complete documentation on how to use LocalMind
GUIDE.START.TITLE: Getting Started
GUIDE.START.INTRO: LocalMind is a local knowledge management system with AI support. It allows you to upload documents, index them semantically, and query them via chat with local or cloud LLM models. Follow these steps to get started.
GUIDE.START.STEP1_DESC: Go to Settings from the sidebar menu and click + Add Provider. To get started quickly locally, select the Ollama type: the system automatically detects models downloaded on your machine and shows them in a dropdown. For cloud providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini) you will need to enter your API Key.
GUIDE.START.STEP2_DESC: Go to the Documents section and upload the files you want to make searchable. Supported formats are PDF, DOCX, DOC, TXT, MD, CSV, and JSON. Documents will be processed automatically: text is extracted, split into chunks, and transformed into vector embeddings for semantic search.
GUIDE.START.STEP3_DESC: Open Chat from the menu. Select the provider and model from the dropdowns at the top, then type your question. The AI can also draw from uploaded documents (RAG mode - Retrieval Augmented Generation).
GUIDE.START.STEP4_DESC: Use Semantic Search to find specific information in indexed documents. You can ask questions in natural language: the system understands the meaning of your request, not just exact words.
GUIDE.START.STEP5_DESC: Configure Monitored Folders to automatically index new files you save in a specific directory. The system checks folders every 15 minutes.
GUIDE.START.NAV_INFO: Navigation: use the sidebar menu to navigate between sections. The sidebar can be collapsed by clicking the arrow at the top. All sections are accessible even when the sidebar is collapsed, thanks to the icons.
GUIDE.DASHBOARD.TITLE: Dashboard
GUIDE.DASHBOARD.INTRO: The Dashboard is the system overview page. It provides an immediate overview of LocalMind's status and shortcuts to the most common operations.
GUIDE.DASHBOARD.SYSTEM_STATUS_DESC: At the top, the backend API status is displayed:
GUIDE.DASHBOARD.UP_DESC: The backend is reachable and functioning. All operations are available.
GUIDE.DASHBOARD.DOWN_DESC: The backend is not responding. Verify the server is running on port 8080.
GUIDE.DASHBOARD.COUNTERS_DESC: The dashboard shows three main counters:
GUIDE.DASHBOARD.COUNTER_DOCS: Documents: total number of documents uploaded to the system (in any status)
GUIDE.DASHBOARD.COUNTER_MCP: MCP Servers: number of MCP servers registered in the configuration
GUIDE.DASHBOARD.COUNTER_LLM: LLM Providers: number of configured and active providers
GUIDE.DASHBOARD.QUICK_ACTIONS_DESC: Four buttons to quickly access the main features:
GUIDE.DASHBOARD.QA_UPLOAD: Upload Documents: go to the documents section to upload new files
GUIDE.DASHBOARD.QA_SEARCH: RAG Search: opens semantic search in indexed documents
GUIDE.DASHBOARD.QA_MCP: MCP Management: opens the MCP server management section
GUIDE.CHAT.TITLE: Chat
GUIDE.CHAT.INTRO: The Chat interface is the heart of LocalMind. It allows you to converse with configured AI models, with the ability to automatically draw from indexed documents for contextualized responses (RAG).
GUIDE.CHAT.SELECT_PROVIDER_DESC: Before sending a message, select the provider and model from the two dropdowns in the chat's top bar. Available providers are those configured in the Settings section. For each provider, available models are shown.
GUIDE.CHAT.ACTION_SEND_HOW: Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> or click the send button
GUIDE.CHAT.ACTION_NEW_CHAT_HOW: Click the New Chat button at the top
GUIDE.CHAT.QUICK_SUGGESTIONS_DESC: When the chat is empty (no messages), clickable suggestions are shown. Clicking a suggestion automatically inserts the text into the input box and sends it. This is useful for starting quickly without typing a question from scratch.
GUIDE.CHAT.HISTORY_DESC: Conversations are saved automatically. In the chat sidebar you can see the list of previous conversations and reopen them by clicking. Each conversation maintains the full history of exchanged messages.
GUIDE.CHAT.RAG_MODE_DESC: When you send a message, the system automatically searches indexed documents for the most relevant passages to your question. These passages are included in the context sent to the AI model, allowing it to provide answers based on your documents. This mode is called Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG).
GUIDE.CHAT.TIP: Tip: to get better answers with RAG, formulate specific questions relevant to the documents you have uploaded. Generic questions will receive generic answers from the model, without references to your data.
GUIDE.DOCUMENTS.TITLE: Documents
GUIDE.DOCUMENTS.INTRO: The Documents section allows you to upload, view, and manage files that feed LocalMind's knowledge base. Uploaded documents are processed and made available for semantic search and RAG in chat.
GUIDE.DOCUMENTS.FORMAT_PDF_NOTE: Documents with extractable text (not scanned images)
GUIDE.DOCUMENTS.UPLOAD_STEP1_DESC: The button is located in the Documents page header.
GUIDE.DOCUMENTS.UPLOAD_STEP2_DESC: Choose a file from your filesystem. Only supported formats are accepted.
GUIDE.DOCUMENTS.UPLOAD_STEP3_DESC: The document goes through several stages: text extraction, chunking, vector embedding generation, and indexing in the vector store.
GUIDE.DOCUMENTS.STATUS_PENDING_DESC: The document has been uploaded but not yet processed. It will be processed shortly.
GUIDE.DOCUMENTS.STATUS_PROCESSING_DESC: The document is being processed: text extraction, chunking, embedding.
GUIDE.DOCUMENTS.STATUS_INDEXED_DESC: Processing completed. The document is ready for semantic search and RAG.
GUIDE.DOCUMENTS.STATUS_FAILED_DESC: Error during processing. Verify the file is valid and not corrupted.
GUIDE.DOCUMENTS.FILTERS_DESC: Above the document list there are tabs to filter by status: All, Pending, Processing, Indexed, Failed. Click a tab to see only documents in that status.
GUIDE.DOCUMENTS.DELETE_DESC: Click the trash icon (red) on the document card. A confirmation dialog will appear. Confirming will permanently remove the document and its embeddings from the system.
GUIDE.DOCUMENTS.DELETE_WARNING: Warning: deleting a document also removes all its embeddings from the vector store. Search results related to that document will no longer be available.
GUIDE.SEARCH.TITLE: Semantic Search
GUIDE.SEARCH.INTRO: Semantic Search allows you to search for information in indexed documents using natural language. Unlike traditional text search, the system understands the meaning of your question and finds the most relevant passages, even if they use different words.
GUIDE.SEARCH.STEP1_DESC: Enter a question or phrase in the search field. Use natural language, as you would with a colleague. Example: "how do you configure two-factor authentication?"
GUIDE.SEARCH.STEP2_DESC: Select how many results you want from the dropdown. Available values: 3, 5, 10, 20. A lower value returns fewer but more relevant results.
GUIDE.SEARCH.RESULT_SOURCE: Source document: the file name the passage comes from
GUIDE.SEARCH.RESULT_SCORE: Relevance score: a percentage bar indicating how relevant the passage is to the question. Higher = more relevant.
GUIDE.SEARCH.RESULT_EXCERPT: Text excerpt: the document passage matching your search
GUIDE.SEARCH.TIP1: Use complete sentences instead of single keywords
GUIDE.SEARCH.TIP2: Be specific in your question: "how to configure SMTP for sending email" works better than "email"
GUIDE.SEARCH.TIP3: If you don't find results, try rephrasing the question with synonyms
GUIDE.SEARCH.TIP4: Start with Top K = 5 and increase if needed
GUIDE.SEARCH.PREREQUISITE: Prerequisite: search only works on documents with INDEXED status. Make sure you have uploaded and completed indexing of at least one document.
GUIDE.FOLDERS.TITLE: Monitored Folders
GUIDE.FOLDERS.INTRO: Monitored Folders allow you to configure local directories on the filesystem that will be automatically scanned to detect and index new documents. This is useful for automating uploads without manual intervention.
GUIDE.FOLDERS.ADD_STEP1_DESC: The button is located in the Folders page header.
GUIDE.FOLDERS.ADD_STEP2_DESC: Enter the absolute path of the folder to monitor.
GUIDE.FOLDERS.ADD_STEP3_DESC: Specify a file pattern to filter the types of files to index (e.g.: *.pdf,*.md,*.txt). Leave empty for all supported formats. Enable "Include subfolders" for recursive scanning.
GUIDE.FOLDERS.STATUS_ACTIVE_DESC: The folder is regularly monitored and functioning.
GUIDE.FOLDERS.STATUS_SYNCING_DESC: Scanning in progress. New files found will be indexed.
GUIDE.FOLDERS.STATUS_ERROR_DESC: Scanning error. Verify the path is valid and accessible.
GUIDE.FOLDERS.CARD_SYNC: Last synchronization: date and time of the last scan
GUIDE.FOLDERS.ACTION_SYNC_DESC: Start an immediate scan of the folder (disabled if already in progress)
GUIDE.FOLDERS.ACTION_DELETE_DESC: Removes the folder configuration from the system
GUIDE.FOLDERS.AUTO_SCAN: Automatic scanning: folders are checked by the backend every 15 minutes. New files matching configured patterns are detected, added to the processing queue, processed (text extraction, chunking, embedding), and indexed in the vector store.
GUIDE.PROVIDERS.TITLE: LLM Provider Settings
GUIDE.PROVIDERS.INTRO: The Settings section allows you to configure the LLM providers used by the system for chat and AI operations. You can add multiple providers, each with its own credentials and default model.
GUIDE.PROVIDERS.ADD_STEP2_DESC: Enter a descriptive name (e.g.: "Local Ollama", "OpenAI Production") and select the type from the dropdown. The base URL and placeholders update automatically.
GUIDE.PROVIDERS.ADD_STEP3_DESC: For OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google the API Key field is required. The key is masked (password field) and saved in the database persistently: you won't need to re-enter it when the system restarts.
GUIDE.PROVIDERS.ADD_STEP4_DESC: For Ollama: the field shows a dropdown automatically populated with models downloaded on your instance. Use the refresh button to reload the list. For cloud providers: type the model name in the text field.
GUIDE.PROVIDERS.ADD_STEP5_DESC: Click "Save Provider". The button is only active when all required fields are filled.
GUIDE.PROVIDERS.CARD_ICON: Type icon: colored circle with the initial (green Ollama, teal OpenAI, brown Anthropic, blue Google)
GUIDE.PROVIDERS.CARD_MODELS: Model list: tags with available models (for Ollama)
GUIDE.PROVIDERS.TEST_DESC: The Test Connection button verifies that the provider is reachable. For Ollama it shows the number of available models. For cloud providers it verifies the API key is configured. The result is communicated via notification at the top of the page.
GUIDE.PROVIDERS.REMOVE_DESC: Click the red Remove button on the provider card. The provider and all its configurations (including the API key) will be deleted from the database.
GUIDE.PROVIDERS.NOTIFICATIONS: Notifications: all operations (add, remove, test) generate colored notifications at the top of the page that automatically disappear after 4 seconds. Green = success, Red = error.
GUIDE.MCP.TITLE: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
GUIDE.MCP.INTRO: The MCP section allows you to register external MCP servers and explore and execute the tools they provide. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard protocol for integrating tools and resources with AI models. The interface is organized in two tabs: External Servers and Available Tools.
GUIDE.MCP.REGISTER_STEP2_DESC: Enter name, description (optional) and select the connection type.
GUIDE.MCP.REGISTER_STEP3_DESC: Based on the selected type, fill in the specific fields (see table below).
GUIDE.MCP.SSE_URL_DESC: SSE endpoint URL of the server
GUIDE.MCP.STATUS_CONNECTED_DESC: The server is connected and functioning
GUIDE.MCP.ACTION_TEST_DESC: Verifies connectivity. Shows spinner during the test and notifies with the result.
GUIDE.MCP.ACTION_RECONNECT_DESC: Attempts reconnection to the server. Shows spinner during the attempt.
GUIDE.MCP.ACTION_DELETE_DESC: Removes the server from the configuration (red button).
GUIDE.MCP.LOCAL_TOOLS_DESC: Local tools are those exposed directly by the LocalMind backend. Each tool is presented as a card with name (monospace font), description and Local badge.
GUIDE.MCP.EXTERNAL_TOOLS_DESC: External tools come from connected MCP servers. Each tool shows name, description, External badge, and abbreviated Server ID. If there are no external tools, it suggests connecting an MCP server.
GUIDE.MCP.EXEC_STEP1_DESC: Click on the tool card you want to execute. It highlights with border and shadow.
GUIDE.MCP.EXEC_STEP2_DESC: In the section that appears below, the name, description, and input schema are shown in JSON format. This schema describes the structure of the arguments required by the tool.
GUIDE.MCP.EXEC_STEP3_DESC: Write the arguments in the text field in JSON format.
GUIDE.MCP.EXEC_STEP4_DESC: The tool is executed and the results are shown in the card.
GUIDE.MCP.RESULTS_DESC: After execution, the following are shown:
GUIDE.MCP.RESULT_DATA: Result data: tool output in JSON format (dark background, monospace font)
GUIDE.MCP.REFRESH_INFO: Refresh: the "Refresh" button in the tab header reloads the list of all available tools (local and external), useful after adding or removing an MCP server.
